newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - NSW budget provides few shocks.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - NSW budget provides few shocks.

text.p: TCV NSW T-CORP QTC
SAFA WATC TASCOR
*The New South Wales 1997/98 budget on Tuesday produced few shocks for the semi-government bond.
*NSW TCorp sees continued demand from Japan.

The New South Wales 1997/98 state budget on Tuesday produced few shocks for the semi-government bond, although the traders said yield spreads to Australian Treasury bonds were showing a tighter bias in the past few days.
"I don't think it's a result of the budget, the market had been trending that way. It's probably the indirect result of renewed (dual currency) samurai supply," one trader said.
Short-dated semis bond usually benefit from the swap-related activity needed to set-up a dual-currency (yen/Australian dollar) samurai, he added.
European Investment Bank issued such a structure on Tuesday.
The New South Wales state government projected a underlying budget surplus of A$27 million for 1997/98 compared with a predicted A$67 million underlying surplus for 1996/97.

Meanwhile, NSW Treasury Corp (TCorp) said its total funding requirement for 1997/98 would be A$4.9 billion, and slightly higher than the previous year reflecting a high level of A$4.6 billion in maturing debt.
"The bottom line is that New South Wales is not going to lose its triple-A rating, even though it's not doing so well as other states," one trader said.
David Thurtell, an analyst at Commonwealth Bank Australia, noted that the state's debt has widened slightly to government bonds since last August's Federal budget.
"However, the spread remains narrow relative to recent years and is expected to remain tight, reflecting ongoing budget surpluses and reductions in debt," he added.

Meanwhile, TCorp said it would access offshore markets for some 40 to 50 percent of its funding in the coming fiscal year and expected continued demand from Japanese investors for its samurai bond issues.

"It's still our preference to tap the Japanese for the bulk of our offshore issuance because it's so attractive," T-Corp's General Manager of Treasury Stephen Knight told reporters earlier on Wednesday.

The Euro-Australian dollar market, along with samurais, are expected to provide the main funding opportunities for issuance, a route TCorp took on Tuesday with a A$100 million 10-year Eurobond through Hambros Bank.
TCorp added that the main focus for the domestic programme would be to be build up its outstanding lines in its 2006 and 2008 stocks.
